source_text: TMP-9021 Action Item Recommendation to approve an interlocal agreement between Reno-Sparks Indian Colony ("RSIC" or "Tribe") and Washoe County, by and through Washoe County Regional Animal Services ("WCRAS"), with a term of three years ; and authorize the Chair of the Board of County Commissioners to execute the agreement. Under this agreement, WCRAS will provide certain animal control and sheltering services for the benefit of the Tribe, including impoundment and care of stray/lost dogs and cats found on Reservation property; disposition of unclaimed dogs and cats; quarantine of dogs and cats that have bitten a person; safehold of dogs and cats in the event of an owner's death; limited field services; and yearly outreach (vaccination) services, with costs to be borne by Tribe as specified in Exhibit A. It is further recommended to authorize the Director of WCRAS to approve and execute annual addendums with amendments to Exhibit A (Costs & Fees) and Article 11 (Notices) as necessary. source_text: TMP-9246 Action Item Declaration of canvass of local results of General Election 2024 and direction to the Registrar of Voters to certify the abstract of the results and transmit a copy of the certified abstract to the Secretary of State. Canvassing is the process by which local election results are declared, examined and certified. The canvass is a culmination of all the data generated during an election cycle. The canvass process aggregates and confirms every valid ballot cast and counted, including mail, uniformed and overseas citizen, electronically transmitted ballots, early voting, and Election Day ballots. NRS 293.387 requires the Board of County Commissioners to separately note any clerical errors discovered and take account of those errors, so the result declared represents the true vote cast. Pursuant to NRS 293.387, the Board of County Commissioners is required to canvass the vote and direct an abstract of votes to be sent to the Secretary of State no later than 10 days following the election, which was held on November 5, 2024. source_snippet: TMP-9630 Action Item Request by the Washoe County Manager, through the Washoe County Clerk, and pursuant to Washoe County Code (“WCC”) 2.030, to initiate amendments to WCC Chapter 5 (Administration and Personnel) to update provisions relating to citizen advisory boards (CABs). The amendments may include, but are not limited to: renaming the boards; clarifying that the purpose of the boards is to provide feedback on community-wide issues within Washoe County’s governmental jurisdiction as part of the commissioner support program; requiring the geographical boundaries of the boards to fall within a single commissioner district; updating provisions for appointment of members; removing the prohibition on CAB members from concurrently serving on the County’s planning commission or board of adjustment; amending various provisions to comply with current open meeting law requirements; and upd...
source_text: TMP-9630 Action Item Request by the Washoe County Manager, through the Washoe County Clerk, and pursuant to Washoe County Code (“WCC”) 2.030, to initiate amendments to WCC Chapter 5 (Administration and Personnel) to update provisions relating to citizen advisory boards (CABs). The amendments may include, but are not limited to: renaming the boards; clarifying that the purpose of the boards is to provide feedback on community-wide issues within Washoe County’s governmental jurisdiction as part of the commissioner support program; requiring the geographical boundaries of the boards to fall within a single commissioner district; updating provisions for appointment of members; removing the prohibition on CAB members from concurrently serving on the County’s planning commission or board of adjustment; amending various provisions to comply with current open meeting law requirements; and updating provisions related to bylaws; and direct the County Clerk to submit the request to the District Attorney’s Office for preparation of a proposed ordinance in accordance with WCC 2.040. source_text: TMP-10190 Public Hearing Public Hearing: For possible action to conduct a Public Hearing under the Tax Equity and Fiscal Responsibility Act ("TEFRA") and adopt a resolution approving the issuance by the National Finance Authority (New Hampshire) of not to exceed $33,000,000 of Lease Revenue Bonds on behalf of NCCS-UNR Fieldhouse Properties LLC (the "Borrower") for purposes of, and as required by, Internal Revenue Code of 1986 Section 147(f), as amended. The bonds or a portion thereof will be "private activity bonds" and "qualified 501(c)(3) bonds" for purposes of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986. The revenue from the bond issuance will be used (a) finance the cost of the design, development, construction and equipping of (i) an approximately 73,700 square foot indoor all sport fieldhouse and related amenities, (ii) an approximately 85,796 square foot outdoor turf football practice field, and (iii) an approximately 106,078 square foot turf intermural field to be located on the campus of the University of Nevada, Reno (collectively, including related site development, utility, equipment and other improvements Not available Not available

source_text: TMP-10280 Resolution Recommendation to accept a 2026 Nevada State Emergency Response Commission (SERC), United We Stand (UWS) grant for [$32,000.00 no County match required]. The UWS grant is intended to improve state and local government planning, training, and response capabilities to react to Acts of Terrorism. If approved, authorize the Local Emergency Planning Committee (LEPC) Chair to execute grant documents and authorize the County Manager or their designee, to sign the Washoe County Sub-Grant Agreements between Washoe County and REMSA Health, per NRS 244.1505 in the amount of [$5,128.00] for one (1) Tactical Rope Access and Rescue Equipment; the Reno Police Department, per NRS 244.1505 in the amount of [$9,318.00] for twelve (12) Avon Protection Voice Unit Gen with Microphone; and Sparks Police Department, per NRS 244.1505, in the amount of [$10,000.00] for four (4) PepperBall Launchers; approve Resolution necessary for same; and direct Finance to make the necessary budget amendments. Project Manager Kevin Selstrum detailed plans to improve the TRI Sheriff’s Office Substation. source_text: 4. Recommended Conditions of Approval A. Special Use Permit. This approval is for Special Use Permit 2026-018 to construct a natural gas fueled electrical generating facility. The electricity generated will be used on adjacent properties owned and/or controlled by the applicant. The project includes onsite storage of compressed natural gas (CNG). The property is located within the Tahoe Reno Industrial Center at 2300 Peru Drive, McCarran, Storey County, NV, Assessor’s Parcel Number 005-012-73. B. Requirements. source_snippet: 2. Representatives of the Union and its affiliates will be permitted to transact Union business on County property, provided that this does not disrupt normal work functions. In accordance with NRS 288, the Employer may require Union business to be conducted during non-work time, such as before work and after work, during breaks, and/or lunchtime. Union business may only be conducted in common areas and/or designated Employee break areas. The designated representative of the Union shall be allowed to receive telephone calls or other communique concerning Union business at any time during working hours. The Union shall have the right to use the interoffice mail for Union business. County email may be used internally to conduct Union business but shall be limited to all parties to this Agreement and subject to established County policies.
source_text: 2. Representatives of the Union and its affiliates will be permitted to transact Union business on County property, provided that this does not disrupt normal work functions. In accordance with NRS 288, the Employer may require Union business to be conducted during non-work time, such as before work and after work, during breaks, and/or lunchtime. Union business may only be conducted in common areas and/or designated Employee break areas. The designated representative of the Union shall be allowed to receive telephone calls or other communique concerning Union business at any time during working hours. The Union shall have the right to use the interoffice mail for Union business. The agreed upon contract covers many benefits which will support the current members along with providing for an attractive package for future recruitment of new members to the Fire District. source_text: • Recommended motion: I, Commissioner (name), move to approve the Interlocal contract and referenced FY 2027 and FY 2028 budgets, as presented. • Prepared by: Maxine Cortes Department: Clerk & Treasurer Contact Number: (775) 283-7249 • Staff Summary: Since 2007, the First Judicial District Court has requested reimbursement from the State of Nevada acting by and through its Department of Health and Human Services to allow Carson City's General Fund to be reimbursed for child support enforcement services conducted in Carson City in lieu of requiring Carson City and Storey County residents to seek enforcement of child support matters in Reno, Nevada. The First Judicial District Court appoints a Child Support Magistrate to preside over the hearings. The Court's Marshals Division provides courtroom security and public screening, and court employees process child support documents. The hearings are conducted at the Murphy-Bernardini Regional Juvenile Justice Center. Every four years, a new Interlocal contract must be agreed upon to continue services and to allow Carson City to receive reimbursement. source_text: 13.118.010 Definitions. As used in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires: "County resident" refers to any individual whose primary and legal place of residence is located within the geographical boundaries of Storey County. Residency may be demonstrated through documentation such as a valid driver’s license or state ID with a Storey County address, a current utility bill, lease or mortgage agreement, voter registration, or other official documents showing name and address within the Storey County. “Immediate Family” means the Storey County Resident’s spouse or domestic partner, parents, children (including stepchildren and legally adopted children), siblings, grandparents, and grandchildren, whether related by blood, marriage, or legal adoption. "Park" means any area designed by the county commissioners as a public park, playground or recreational facility pursuant to Section 13.118.050 of this chapter. source_text: 13.118.040 Compliance required. A. No person shall enter, be or remain in any park or swimming pool of the county as designated by the county commissioners by resolution pursuant to this chapter unless he/she complies they comply with this chapter and the regulations promulgated by this chapter and any resolution adopted pursuant thereto. B. The Storey County sheriff is authorized to eject and expel from a park and the swimming pool any person who violates the provisions of this chapter or any other law, ordinance, or park resolution that may be in effect at the time of such violation. C. Ejected or Expelled Persons. No person who has been ejected or expelled under the provisions of this section shall refuse to leave any park or swimming pool as ordered nor shall the person return to the park or swimming pool within twenty-four hours of such ejection or expulsion without the permission of the Storey County sheriff. D. Violation: Penalty. Any person who violates the provisions contained in this chapter or any park resolution adopted pursuant thereto is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine not to exceed one thousand dollars, imprisonment not to exceed six months, or both....

source_snippet: 4. Staff summary: This resolution is in recognition of the lifesaving efforts made by Storey County Fire District Firefighter Jesse Richardson. On July 26th Jesse responded along with his partner Charlie Bowman to a fire on Lousetown Road with a report of a victim trapped. While Charlie attempted access to the interior of the structure, Jesse carried a 24’ ladder around to the C side of the structure locating the victim on the balcony. He placed the ladder and even utilized a rock to stabilize it due to the angle. He then ascended the ladder and assisted the resident over the railing and down to safety. Without his efforts, the outcome could have been fatal.
source_text: 4. Staff summary: This resolution is in recognition of the lifesaving efforts made by Storey County Fire District Firefighter Jesse Richardson. On July 26th Jesse responded along with his partner Charlie Bowman to a fire on Lousetown Road with a report of a victim trapped. While Charlie attempted access to the interior of the structure, Jesse carried a 24’ ladder around to the C side of the structure locating the victim on the balcony. He placed the ladder and even utilized a rock to stabilize it due to the angle. He then ascended the ladder and assisted the resident over the railing and down to safety. Without his efforts, the outcome could have been fatal.

source_text: III. Conclusion For these reasons, Sunny Hills respectfully requests that the County decline to process or consider the SUP Application unless and until NV Energy demonstrates that it has obtained the requisite property owner authorizations for all affected properties. At a minimum, the County should continue consideration of the SUP Application until NV Energy identifies with specificity the parcels through which the Mira Loma Corridor is proposed to pass and the corresponding property interests necessary for the Project. Although the Commission should decline to consider the application, if it is nonetheless inclined to approve the application, the condition should go further. Not only should the SUP be conditioned on no construction proceeding without an easement or authorization, but the SUP should be revokable if NV Energy does not obtain the necessary property interests. The property owners should have the right to contest the SUP and petition it be revoked to remove the encumbrance on their properties. Sunny Hills further requests that this correspondence and the objections set forth herein be incorporated into the administrative record and considered by the Planning Comm...

It is in Chapter 5, which doesn’t really have anything to do with Planning, but the code talks a little bit about land uses. Main St. The Preliminary Plat for Great Basin Estates was also approved, and the Final Plat for that subdivision will go on the June 14, 2016 Meeting. source_text: recommendation to the Redevelopment Agency to establish a storefront improvement reimbursement program. As you know we did have that storefront program, it was a grant program that was federally funded. It was de-obligated from the funds by City Council. They have reached out to the Redevelopment Agency of Nevada and have meeting with them quarterly. There are several communities in the state that have done these storefront improvement reimbursement programs. They are going to reach out to them and get as much information from them as possible and learn from their trial and errors. The Redevelopment Advisory Council recommended to the Redevelopment Agency a program of $50,000 a year maximum expenditure up to five years, reevaluate the program at the five years. They also recommended a maximum of $10,000 reimbursement per property owner. That will go to the RDA at 2:30 pm on August 9, 2016. Commissioner Negrete asked if there was a minimum amount that could be applied for. Ms. Laughlin answered that this item was just to establish the storefront program. For Possible Action: Discussion and Possible Action to approve a renewal proposal from Nevada Public Agency Insurance Pool (POOL) and Approval for Payment from Fiscal Year 2026-2027 funds. City Manager Bryant stated that we have Wayne Carlson and Tina Pederson to present here today. This is an annual item that pops up every year and this is our annual renewal. Tina Pederson stated that there are some changes this year. Property insurance was increased. You, as a member, have say on what the insurance provides. Article 22 has been amended to state that any member giving 120-day notice of withdrawal waives the two-thirds penalty fee. Now I’ll talk about the savings. There is an overall decrease of -13.23%. source_text: 4. Step Three: If the grievance is not resolved at Step Two of the procedure, and the grievant desires to submit the dispute to the Yerington City Council for final resolution, the time for his/her appeal shall begin with the receipt of the response of the Yerington City Manager. Within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of the written answer by the Yerington City Manager, the aggrieved party may appeal the decision to the Yerington City Council filing with the Yerington City Clerk a written statement of his/her intention to appeal, including sufficient details of circumstances surrounding the grievance. Grievance appeals shall be heard by the Yerington City Council and their finding shall be final and conclusive. Following notice of appeal, the Yerington City Clerk shall immediately notify the Mayor of the City of Yerington. If the date of the next regularly scheduled meeting of the Council is more than fifteen (15) calendar days from the date of the appeal is filed, the appeal shall be heard at the earliest possible date established by the Council.

source_text: 15. For Discussion Only: Discussion of Resolution 2026-07, a Resolution amending the City of Yerington Fee Schedule Water Standpipe Rates. This item was first publicly discussed by Yerington City Council at the March 23, 2026 regular meeting. Interim City Manager Bryant discusses the recently approved meter system. We hope to see this implemented soon to help streamline our services. This item is to consider amending the fee schedule to reflect a $5.00 per thousand gallon model at the J-stand water distribution location. Currently, we charge $38.00 for the first fifteen thousand gallons and a commodity rate of just over $2 per thousand gallons thereafter. Bryant proposes removing this model and going to the flat $5.00 per thousand gallons. Mr. Bryant also suggests adding a $100 start-up fee for new accounts to account for the time and staff spent on creating new accounts. Additionally, reactivating a PIN or re-opening after an account lockout for things such as non-payment will now incur a $25.00 fee. -- 25 of 61 -- There was no further discussion on this item.

For the County to get full use of the grant they would have to spend $6,000 a month on maintenance to the senior vans. source_text: Operating Assistance 50/50 grant. Commissioner Plaskett seconded the motion. The motion carried 3-0. THE EUREKA SENTINEL- Ben Rowley, Owner/ Publisher

source_snippet: meeting. (For Possible Action) CIO Misty Rowley explained that during the implementation of Ironclad they discovered they needed more power user licenses to cover multiple people in the offices. They started with 20 users, and the increase will bring them to 32. CIO Rowley also requested the Board approve her to add or remove licenses as necessary. Commissioner Plaskett motioned to approve the addition of 12 Ironclad Power User licenses at a rate of $600 per user per year to the existing three-year term (January 20, 2026 through September 1, 2028). Also to authorize CIO Rowley to add or remove licenses as necessary and to execute the Order Form outside of the meeting. Commissioner Schoenwald seconded the motion. The motion carried 3-0. COUNTY FACILITIES – Brenna Rogne, Facilities/Events Manager
source_text: meeting. (For Possible Action) CIO Misty Rowley explained that during the implementation of Ironclad they discovered they needed more power user licenses to cover multiple people in the offices. They started with 20 users, and the increase will bring them to 32. CIO Rowley also requested the Board approve her to add or remove licenses as necessary. Commissioner Plaskett motioned to approve the addition of 12 Ironclad Power User licenses at a rate of $600 per user per year to the existing three-year term (January 20, 2026 through September 1, 2028). Also to authorize CIO Rowley to add or remove licenses as necessary and to execute the Order Form outside of the meeting. Commissioner Schoenwald seconded the motion. The motion carried 3-0. COUNTY FACILITIES – Brenna Rogne, Facilities/Events Manager

Commissioner Plaskett seconded the motion. The motion carried 3-0.

source_text: Thompson Reuters will replace Trans Union Risk and Alternative. (For Possible Action) The Sheriff’s office was using Trans Union Risk and Alternative for background checks and investigations; Trans Union was more eastern based and cost $1,100 monthly. Thompson Reuters is western based and will cost $211 monthly. Commissioner Schoenwald motioned to approve entering into a 3-year contract with Thompson Reuters (Clear for LE, investigative resource) in the amount of $211.00 a month for the first year with a 5% increase in years 2 & 3 and authorize the Sheriff’s Department to sign contract outside of the meeting. Commissioner Plaskett seconded the motion. The motion carried 3-0. ROAD DEPARTMENT – Scooter Mentaberry, Supervisor

source_text: 1. Review, discuss and provide direction to the Comptroller related to proposed cost of living adjustments for Non-PERS and PERS employees, effective July 5, 2026. Note: Union contracts have not been approved for next year so COLA increase is unknown at this time. Elected Officials are limited to a 2% increase, County Commissioners are limited to a 3% increase. (For Possible Action) At the previous Commission meeting during the budget session the board chose to not approve a COLA increase for the County Commissioners, Comptroller Kim Todd informed the board that due to a new legislative bill they unfortunately can not approve some but not all. In order to follow new legislature the board either approves a COLA increase for all non-PERS and PERS employees, elected officials and County Commissioners or none at all. Commissioner Schoenwald motioned to approve a 2% COLA for elected officials, 3% for County Commissioners, 3% COLA for hourly employees and $0.25 increase for casual positions. Commissioner Plaskett seconded the motion. The motion carried 3-0.

source_snippet: (For Possible Action) The proposed changes to the Eureka County Personnel Policy: Leave Plans, 6.1 Holidays are: Employees participating in the 4x10 pilot program shall follow the existing Holiday Leave policy applicable to 10-hour workdays, except as modify below. For Offices required by Nevada law to remain operational, including elected official offices: If a federally recognized holiday falls on a Friday or Saturday, the elected official or department head may coordinate with employees to schedule an alternate day off. Any such holiday leave must be taken within the same work week in which the holiday occurs, ensuring that operational coverage is maintained. Commissioner Plaskett motioned to approve the changes to Eureka County Personnel Policy: Leave Plans, 6.1 Holidays. Commissioner Schoenwald seconded the motion. The motion carried 3- IT – Misty Rowley, CIO

Any such holiday leave must be taken within the same work week in which the holiday occurs, ensuring that operational coverage is maintained. Commissioner Plaskett motioned to approve the changes to Eureka County Personnel Policy: Leave Plans, 6.1 Holidays. Commissioner Schoenwald seconded the motion. The motion carried 3- IT – Misty Rowley, CIO

source_text: Commission Department (010-019-53010-000). (For Possible Action) -- 14 of 164 -- Page 12 of 13- May 19, 2026 The current Eureka County Master Plan has not been updated since 2010, Nevada’s Statute covers the requirement for a county to maintain a master plan that guides land use, growth management, infrastructure, economic development, natural resources, water resources and transportation. The Hazard Mitigation plan and other economic development planning is being updated, Director Rowley believes now would be a good time to include the Master Plan. Commissioner Plaskett motioned to approve a Contracted Services Agreement and Scope of Work between Eureka County and Nevada Strategies LLC for development of the Eureka County Master Plan and general planning advisory services for a term of twelve (12) months at $10,000.00 per month, for a total contract amount not to exceed $120,000.00, utilizing funds budgeted for contract services in the Public Works Department (010-042-53010-058) and services and supplies in the Planning Commission Department (010-019-53010-000). Commissioner Schoenwald seconded the motion. The motion carried 3-0. CORRESPONDENCE

source_snippet: Operating Assistance 50/50 grant. (For Possible Action) Senior Center Program Director Linda Gordon presented to the board sending a letter to Nevada Department of Transportation forgoing the FTA Section 5310, FEY25-26 Funding Application Operating Assistance 50/50 grant. For the County to get full use of the grant they would have to spend $6,000 a month on maintenance to the senior vans. Director Gordon did not believe they use the vans enough to justify $6,000 a month when the vans are used a handful of times a month. Commissioner Schoenwald motioned to approve Senior Center Program Director Linda Gordon sending a letter to Nevada Department of Transportation forgoing the FTA Section 5310, FEY25-26 Funding Application Operating Assistance 50/50 grant. Commissioner Plaskett seconded the motion. The motion carried 3-0. THE EUREKA SENTINEL- Ben Rowley, Owner/ Publisher
source_text: Operating Assistance 50/50 grant. (For Possible Action) Senior Center Program Director Linda Gordon presented to the board sending a letter to Nevada Department of Transportation forgoing the FTA Section 5310, FEY25-26 Funding Application Operating Assistance 50/50 grant. For the County to get full use of the grant they would have to spend $6,000 a month on maintenance to the senior vans. Director Gordon did not believe they use the vans enough to justify $6,000 a month when the vans are used a handful of times a month. Commissioner Schoenwald motioned to approve Senior Center Program Director Linda Gordon sending a letter to Nevada Department of Transportation forgoing the FTA Section 5310, FEY25-26 Funding Application Operating Assistance 50/50 grant. Commissioner Plaskett seconded the motion. The motion carried 3-0. THE EUREKA SENTINEL- Ben Rowley, Owner/ Publisher

(For Possible Action) CIO Misty Rowley explained that during the implementation of Ironclad they discovered they needed more power user licenses to cover multiple people in the offices. They started with 20 users, and the increase will bring them to 32. CIO Rowley also requested the Board approve her to add or remove licenses as necessary. Commissioner Plaskett motioned to approve the addition of 12 Ironclad Power User licenses at a rate of $600 per user per year to the existing three-year term (January 20, 2026 through September 1, 2028). Also to authorize CIO Rowley to add or remove licenses as necessary and to execute the Order Form outside of the meeting. Commissioner Schoenwald seconded the motion. The motion carried 3-0. source_text: 3. Review, discuss and provide direction to the Comptroller related to proposed cost of living adjustments for Non-PERS and PERS employees, effective July 5, 2026. Note: Union contracts have not been approved for next year so COLA increase is unknown at this time. Elected Officials are limited to a 2% increase, County Commissioners are limited to a 3% increase. (For Possible The County Elected Officials are limited to a 2% cost of living adjustment (COLA) increase and the County Commissioners are limited to a 3% increase. The Board discussed a 3% increase for hourly employees, a $0.25 increase for casuals and chose to not take an increase for the Commissioners. Commissioner Schoenwald motioned to approve a 0% cost of living adjustment (COLA) increase for the Commissioners, 2% COLA for elected officials, 3% COLA for hourly employees and $0.25 increase for casual positions. Commissioner Plaskett seconded the motion. The motion carried 3-0.

source_text: 1. Review, discuss and provide direction to the Comptroller related to proposed cost of living adjustments for Non-PERS and PERS employees, effective July 5, 2026. Note: Union contracts have not been approved for next year so COLA increase is unknown at this time. Elected Officials are limited to a 2% increase, County Commissioners are limited to a 3% increase. (For Possible Action) At the previous Commission meeting during the budget session the board chose to not approve a COLA increase for the County Commissioners, Comptroller Kim Todd informed the board that due to a new legislative bill they unfortunately can not approve some but not all. In order to follow new legislature the board either approves a COLA increase for all non-PERS and PERS employees, elected officials and County Commissioners or none at all. Commissioner Schoenwald motioned to approve a 2% COLA for elected officials, 3% for County Commissioners, 3% COLA for hourly employees and $0.25 increase for casual positions. Commissioner Plaskett seconded the motion. The motion carried 3-0.

source_text: Process in lieu of Hiring Freeze Resolution. (For Possible Action) Director Lopez explained when it comes to revenue the County doesn’t need to put a hiring freeze in place, looking into the future they want to make sure that all positions are reviewed prior to approval or postings. Kim Todd commented on proposed changes to the draft Workforce Position Control and Vacancy Review Process in lieu of Hiring Freeze Resolution; adding if the position was budgeted for and what year, adding additional costs that a department head would not know about, get rid of the county manager authorization spot due to the county manager position being removed. Rewording that the Commissioners “shall” confirm funding with the Comptroller’s office, she also believes the board should always have the opportunity to authorize layoffs due to never knowing what kind of financial burden they may face. Vice Chair Plaskett commented the layoff section was meant to say that the resolution was not intended for layoffs. The board discussed proposed changes and re-wording of certain areas and bringing the resolution back onto a future agenda. No action was taken. TREASURER – Pernecia, Johnson, Treasurer

source_text: Impact Statement. (For Possible Action) The original record of decision was signed in 2012 and was appealed by an environmental group and a farming family in Diamond Valley; the 9th circuit vacated the case back to the BLM to address issues. The supplemental EIS process was issued a second record of decision in 2019 that was again appealed, the case went to the federal district court and eventually General Moly went bankrupt and a new company called New Molly LLC is continuing the case. The new Mount Hope Project Environmental Impact Statement discusses the amended plan of operation and redesigns facilities to avoid any use of occupancy of the withdrawn lands; however, the plan does not discuss how it will conform with the Greater Sage Grouse plans. The Board discussed reviewing the BLM state directors review of the record of decision and sending a letter to the company asking to reengage in conversations reminding them of their commitments to Eureka County. source_snippet: (For Possible Action) The proposed changes to the Eureka County Personnel Policy: Leave Plans, 6.1 Holidays are: Employees participating in the 4x10 pilot program shall follow the existing Holiday Leave policy applicable to 10-hour workdays, except as modify below. For Offices required by Nevada law to remain operational, including elected official offices: If a federally recognized holiday falls on a Friday or Saturday, the elected official or department head may coordinate with employees to schedule an alternate day off. Any such holiday leave must be taken within the same work week in which the holiday occurs, ensuring that operational coverage is maintained. Commissioner Plaskett motioned to approve the changes to Eureka County Personnel Policy: Leave Plans, 6.1 Holidays. Commissioner Schoenwald seconded the motion. The motion carried 3- IT – Misty Rowley, CIO

Any such holiday leave must be taken within the same work week in which the holiday occurs, ensuring that operational coverage is maintained. Commissioner Plaskett motioned to approve the changes to Eureka County Personnel Policy: Leave Plans, 6.1 Holidays. Commissioner Schoenwald seconded the motion. The motion carried 3- IT – Misty Rowley, CIO

Manager Tibbitts gave a presentation to the Diamond Valley Groundwater Management Plan on the results of the Mining and Land Resource -- 12 of 299 -- Page 9 of 11- April 21, 2026 Institute meeting. Manager Tibbitts attended a meeting with ORLA Mining about the South Railroad project, they discussed the concerns Pine Valley residents had on the water issues, he believes they will be removing their protests on the water applications. Manager Tibbitts reminded the board Firewise days will be May 1st in Eureka and May 2nd in Crescent Valley.

source_snippet: 2. Pledge of Allegiance. The Board of Eureka County Commissioners met pursuant to law on May 5, 2026. Present were Chairman Rich McKay, Vice Chair Marty Plaskett, Commissioner Mike Schoenwald via Webex, District Attorney Ted Beutel and Deputy Clerk Recorder Katelyn Ziemann. The miscellaneous budget remained the same, it pays for tax liability, leave payouts, insurance and COBRA. Juvenile Probation decreased $800. District Attorney increased $11,000. Lisa Wolf in Crescent Valley asked if the ordinance would affect the growing of hemp. Robin Hicks questioned the law of allowing 1 business in the county. Chairman McKay explained based on Eureka Counties population there can only be 1 marijuana business. Garney Damele with the Eureka Sentinel asked why the ordinance is tied to a specific date and how easily it would be to amend the date. District Attorney Beutel answered that the date is tied to the lawsuit. Laurell Marshall asked if the ordinance could include geographic restrictions saying it couldn’t be a certain distance from a school, child care facility or church. (For Possible Action) Health Insurance Advisory Board member Jayme Halpin reported LP Insurance contacted them and reported Prominence Health Insurance was doing away with Cigna network, which is all the out-of- state providers. LP Insurance went out to market and received competitive quotes; Anthem Insurance came back with the best plan. source_text: America 250 Project. (For Possible Action) The Charters of Freedom America 250 Project has donated to Eureka County fully engraved, stainless-steel replicas of the Declaration of Independence, US Constitution, Bill of Rights, and Civil Rights Amendments. The board along with Eureka citizens in the audience and members of the Eureka VFW discussed where the best location would be. The board chose the VFW Park for the location of the replicas; they discussed bringing the cost of the project to a later meeting but in the meantime direct NACO to work with Public Works Assistant Director Lester Porter for the delivery of the replicas. Commissioner Plaskett motioned to approve the VFW Park as the location for the replicas of the Declaration of Independence, US Constitution, Bill of Rights, and Civil Rights Amendments gifted to Eureka County by The Charters of Freedom America 250 Project, also to work further details with Eldon Allred with the VFW and Lester Porter. Commissioner Schoenwald seconded the motion. The motion carried 3-0.

These activities will enhance program effectiveness and build capacity within the team. (Facilities Director, Doug Homestead) The two sculptures are as follows: 1. A 53 inch tall railroad spike cast in bronze with the word "Community" engraved on each of the four sides in four languages, one to a side. The second sculpture was donated by a grant and was chosen by the townspeople. It is a concrete obelisk with colorful bas- relief images that relate to the history and culture of the area. Both are funded by Dust and Wonder Trail, a nonprofit working to create a cultural corridor for locals and tourists. https://www.dustandwonder.org/ Please find associated materials that were emailed to further describe the donations, the foundations needed, and the desired locations in the Park. Lumos & Associates recently completed a condition assessment of LS1 and identified significant deterioration of both the wet well structure and the approximately 640-linear-foot gravity sewer main that conveys influent flow beneath the Carson River. source_text: For Possible Action: Approve the Lyon County Personnel Policy Manual with proposed revisions. Proposed revisions include: increase the period from 60 to 90 days as the time within which an employee must use compensatory time; change the definition for which employees are entitled to shift differential; increase vacation accrual from 40 hours to 80 hours for the first year; change various definitions; add a requirement that employees on administrative leave remain available for work; and other minor language clarifications, with all proposed revisions to be effective beginning July 1, 2026. (Human Resources Director, Ben Evans). Significant Changes: Increase compensatory time use time from 90 days to 120 calendar days. Defined only regular staff qualify for a shift differential. Increase vacation accrual from 40 hours to 80 hours during the first year of employment with the County. Defined requirements for personnel to qualify for personal day. Defined employees must exhaust all applicable paid time off before LWOP may be taken. Defined "regular commute distance" for mileage reimbursement purposes. source_text: 5.4.1 Lead Agency Coordination If a project advances beyond the concept planning phase, the lead agency for design and construction will typically be the County in which the project is located. The County would generally be responsible for project scoping, consultant procurement, local coordination, funding applications, design management, public outreach, permitting support, bidding, contract management, and construction administration. However, since these projects directly affect a Nevada State Route, NDOT coordination will be required. Depending on project location, funding source, ownership, maintenance responsibility, and anticipated impacts to state highway infrastructure, NDOT may serve as either a coordinating agency, review agency, funding partner, or lead agency. If NDOT cost-share participation is available, the County and NDOT should determine early in the implementation process which agency will lead project delivery.

Federal requirements may include, but are not limited to, environmental documentation, right-of-way certification, utility coordination, disadvantaged business enterprise requirements, Buy America provisions, competitive procurement, construction contract administration, documentation, and reimbursement procedures. source_text: 5.4.2 Federal-Aid Funding Considerations If Federal-aid Highway Program funds are used, the project must be developed in accordance with applicable federal requirements. In that case, NDOT would typically coordinate with FHWA to manage federal participation, ensure compliance with Federal-aid procedures, and administer required approvals. Federal requirements may include, but are not limited to, environmental documentation, right-of-way certification, utility coordination, disadvantaged business enterprise requirements, Buy America provisions, competitive procurement, construction contract administration, documentation, and reimbursement procedures. Early identification of the funding source is important because federal funding can affect project schedule, documentation requirements, procurement methods, and agency roles. Projects should not proceed into final design or construction advertisement until the applicable funding and compliance requirements are clearly established. -- 172 of 706 --

source_text: 7. NAC 477 – State Fire Marshall Under NAC 477.740, the Nevada State Fire Marshal Division is required to review fire-safety plans for certain building and construction projects to ensure compliance with the State’s adopted fire codes. This includes any building, construction project, or fire-protection system involving public occupancy in a county with a population under 100,000 when no interlocal agreement exists between the State Fire Marshal and the authority having jurisdiction (AHJ). Because Lyon County remains under 100,000 population, the regulation directly applies. If a project is submitted in an area outside the jurisdiction of a local fire-protection district, and the County does not have an interlocal agreement that delegates review authority, then the County must forward those plans to the State Fire Marshal for review and issuance of the required certificate of compliance. A structure cannot be occupied until the State Fire Marshal has issued this certificate. Furthermore, Lyon County’s adoption of the 2024 IFC and Northern Nevada Amendments to the IFC would align county code with the State Fire Marshall standards.

Lyon County does not typically conduct plan reviews or inspections for fire code compliance, except in limited circumstances involving development located outside the jurisdictional boundaries of local fire protection districts. As a result, the adoption of the updated fire code provisions does not appear likely to create additional staffing requirements, operational burdens, or ongoing fiscal obligations for the County. source_text: For Possible Action: Approve the services of independent contractor Candice Landa, LCSW, in an amount not to exceed $84,500, to provide Behavioral Health Clinician services for the Lyon County Resilient Families (LCRF) program. The Lyon County Resilient Families (LCRF) Program performs evidence based assessments to determine need and level of care, targeted case management, prevention and early intervention, evidenced based parent education on substance use, and wrap around linkage to services for youth and families in Lyon County who are affected by Opioid Use Disorder (OUD) or at risk of OUD. Case Management and linkage to care is provided for members of families as well as treatment connection for individuals age 16 and over, with special consideration for transitional aged youth, and those involved or at risk for being involved with the criminal justice or juvenile justice system. The services of Candice Landa, LCSW will be up to 25 hours weekly to provide the Behavioral Health Clinician role for the LCRF program as covered in the State of Nevada, Health and Human Services, Directorâ€™s Office Fund for a Resilient Nevada grant award. It requires an initial noise study and a pre-occupancy verification test. These limits are too permissive for rural Lyon County, particularly where existing nighttime ambient sound may be far lower. The draft also addresses only dBA, which can understate the low-frequency hum, tones, pulsation, and vibration generated by fans, transformers, chillers, and generators. The draft permits an onsite natural-gas power facility as an accessory use if its capacity does not exceed 125% of the data center’s maximum electric demand. source_text: 5. Do not treat a 125%-sized natural-gas plant as an accessory use This is one of the most serious issues in the ordinance. The draft permits an onsite natural-gas power facility as an accessory use if its capacity does not exceed 125% of the data center’s maximum electric demand. For a 500 MW data center, that could allow a 625 MW generating facility to be characterized as “accessory.” That is not a minor or subordinate use. It could function as a major power plant with:  Combustion turbines or reciprocating engines.  Gas pipelines and compression facilities.  Major air emissions.  Continuous noise and vibration.  Cooling infrastructure.  Hazardous-material storage.  Fire and explosion risks.  Significant water use.  New transmission infrastructure. Recommended revision Any onsite generation exceeding the lesser of:  10% of the data center’s maximum demand, or  emergency-only generation capacity,  should be deemed a principal power-generation use requiring a separate CUP. The ordinance should prohibit routine baseload operation under the label of “backup,” “peak reduction,” or “grid stabilization.” It should also require:  Annual operating-hour limits. -- 29 of 166...

source_text: 9. Strengthen water protections The proposed ordinance contains one of its strongest provisions by prohibiting evaporative, adiabatic, open-loop, and other water-consuming cooling systems unless reclaimed or treated effluent is exclusively used under a binding agreement lasting at least 20 years. That protection should be retained, but it needs additional controls. Recommended additions Require the applicant to disclose:  Annual gallons and acre-feet.  Peak-day and peak-hour demand.  Water use effectiveness.  Potable, reclaimed, and process-water quantities separately.  Water consumed by cooling, humidification, domestic use, fire systems, landscaping, power generation, and maintenance.  Water demand during drought and extreme heat.  Chemical additives and blowdown composition.  Source reliability during drought or utility interruption.  A fixed enforceable annual water-use cap.  Separate meters for each source and use.  Monthly reporting.  Public annual water-use reports.  Automatic reopening of the CUP for exceedances.  No potable groundwater for cooling. -- 33 of 166 -- Review of Lyon County’s Proposed Data Center Ordinance

source_text: 1. Setbacks A major concern I have with the ordinance is the proposed setbacks. The ordinance would allow data center buildings and emergency generators to be just 150 feet from homes. Substations could be 200 feet away, and battery energy storage systems and natural gas power facilities could be as close as 250 feet. How were these distances determined? The ordinance does not show that they are based on air pollution studies, health studies, noise studies, battery fire risks, emergency response times, or any other scientific evidence showing these distances are safe. A fence, wall, or landscaped buffer may hide the facility from view, but it does not stop air pollution, diesel exhaust, fine particulate matter (PM2.5), chemical releases, low-frequency noise, vibration, or contaminated smoke if there is a fire. Families should not have to live just a few hundred feet away from a massive industrial facility that operates 24 hours a day and stores large amounts of fuel, batteries, electrical equipment, and cooling chemicals.

source_text: The ordinance should also include stronger operating standards. The County should: Require pollution prevention before pollution control. The goal should not simply be to meet the minimum legal requirements. The goal should be to prevent unnecessary air pollution whenever possible. Prohibit diesel generators from being used for peak shaving, routine grid support, demand response, power sales, or reducing operating costs. Allow diesel generators only during a true power outage or limited maintenance and testing. Set enforceable limits on generator numbers, testing hours, operating hours, fuel use, and total emissions. Require testing to be staggered so multiple facilities are not operating generators at the same time. Require the cleanest available engines, pollution controls, and fuels. Simply labeling an engine "Tier 4" should not end the review. Require battery storage or other non-combustion backup systems whenever they can safely replace diesel generators. Diesel generators should be the last option, not the first.

The Lyon County Resilient Families (LCRF) Program performs evidence based assessments to determine need and level of care, targeted case management, prevention and early intervention, evidenced based parent education on substance use, and wrap around linkage to services for youth and families in Lyon County who are affected by Opioid Use Disorder (OUD) or at risk of OUD. source_text: For Possible Action: Approve the services of independent contractor Candice Landa, LCSW, in an amount not to exceed $84,500, to provide Behavioral Health Clinician services for the Lyon County Resilient Families (LCRF) program. The Lyon County Resilient Families (LCRF) Program performs evidence based assessments to determine need and level of care, targeted case management, prevention and early intervention, evidenced based parent education on substance use, and wrap around linkage to services for youth and families in Lyon County who are affected by Opioid Use Disorder (OUD) or at risk of OUD. Case Management and linkage to care is provided for members of families as well as treatment connection for individuals age 16 and over, with special consideration for transitional aged youth, and those involved or at risk for being involved with the criminal justice or juvenile justice system. The services of Candice Landa, LCSW will be up to 25 hours weekly to provide the Behavioral Health Clinician role for the LCRF program as covered in the State of Nevada, Health and Human Services, Directorâ€™s Office Fund for a Resilient Nevada grant award. Today, NRH serves Nevada’s 15 rural counties and the rural portions of Clark and Washoe counties — a service area spanning more than 110,000 square miles. source_text: For Possible Action: Accept a grant award from the Nevada Department of Health and Human Services for the FY27 Nevada Clinical Services - Respite program, in the amount of $80,271. This is the annual grant renewal for the Nevada Clinical Services â€“ Respite Program through the Nevada Department of Health and Human Services. source_text: For Possible Action: To approve an agreement with Sierra Controls, in an amount not to exceed $160,216.25, to migrate the Silver Springs Wastewater Treatment Plant's existing SCADA system to a new SCADA platform. (Utilities Director, Sean Sinclair) The utility-wide SCADA system has experienced ongoing reliability issues, and the FY27 budget includes funding for a SCADA Improvement Project. Before the project could begin, an electrical storm caused a complete failure of the SCADA computer at the Silver Springs Plant, significantly impacting plant operations. To restore reliable operational control, staff and the Consultant recommend beginning the SCADA improvement work at Silver Springs immediately. The work will include replacing the failed computers and migrating the existing system to the recommended Ignition SCADA platform. The upgraded system can later be integrated into the utility-wide SCADA network as improvements are completed at other facilities. Sierra Controls, the utilityâ€™s SCADA consultant, will provide the hardware and software, perform the migration, and train utility staff. source_text: For Possible Action: To approve an agreement with Sierra Controls, in an amount not to exceed $160,216.25, to migrate the Silver Springs Wastewater Treatment Plant's existing SCADA system to a new SCADA platform. (Utilities Director, Sean Sinclair) The utility-wide SCADA system has experienced ongoing reliability issues, and the FY27 budget includes funding for a SCADA Improvement Project. Before the project could begin, an electrical storm caused a complete failure of the SCADA computer at the Silver Springs Plant, significantly impacting plant operations. To restore reliable operational control, staff and the Consultant recommend beginning the SCADA improvement work at Silver Springs immediately. The work will include replacing the failed computers and migrating the existing system to the recommended Ignition SCADA platform. The upgraded system can later be integrated into the utility-wide SCADA network as improvements are completed at other facilities. Sierra Controls, the utilityâ€™s SCADA consultant, will provide the hardware and software, perform the migration, and train utility staff.
